# gron

Make JSON greppable!

gron transforms JSON into discrete assignments to make it easier to `grep` for what you want and see the absolute 'path' to it.
It eases the exploration of APIs that return large blobs of JSON but have terrible documentation.

## Example

```
▶ gron "https://api.github.com/repos/tomnomnom/gron/commits?per_page=1" | fgrep "commit.author"
json[0].commit.author = {};
json[0].commit.author.date = "2016-07-02T10:51:21Z";
json[0].commit.author.email = "mail@tomnomnom.com";
json[0].commit.author.name = "Tom Hudson";
```

gron can work backwards too, enabling you to turn your filtered data back into JSON:

```
▶ gron "https://api.github.com/repos/tomnomnom/gron/commits?per_page=1" | fgrep "commit.author" | gron --ungron
[
  {
    "commit": {
      "author": {
        "date": "2016-07-02T10:51:21Z",
        "email": "mail@tomnomnom.com",
        "name": "Tom Hudson"
      }
    }
  }
]
```

## Usage

Get JSON from a file:

```
▶ gron testdata/two.json 
json = {};
json.contact = {};
json.contact.email = "mail@tomnomnom.com";
json.contact.twitter = "@TomNomNom";
json.github = "https://github.com/tomnomnom/";
json.likes = [];
json.likes[0] = "code";
json.likes[1] = "cheese";
json.likes[2] = "meat";
json.name = "Tom";
```

From a URL:

```
▶ gron http://headers.jsontest.com/
json = {};
json.Host = "headers.jsontest.com";
json["User-Agent"] = "gron/0.1";
json["X-Cloud-Trace-Context"] = "6917a823919477919dbc1523584ba25d/11970839830843610056";
```

Or from `stdin`:

```
▶ curl -s http://headers.jsontest.com/ | gron
json = {};
json.Accept = "*/*";
json.Host = "headers.jsontest.com";
json["User-Agent"] = "curl/7.43.0";
json["X-Cloud-Trace-Context"] = "c70f7bf26661c67d0b9f2cde6f295319/13941186890243645147";
```

Grep for something and easily see the path to it:

```
▶ gron testdata/two.json | grep twitter
json.contact.twitter = "@TomNomNom";
```

gron makes diffing JSON easy too:

```
▶ diff <(gron two.json) <(gron two-b.json)
3c3
< json.contact.email = "mail@tomnomnom.com";
---
> json.contact.email = "contact@tomnomnom.com";
```

The output of `gron` is valid JavaScript:

```
▶ gron testdata/two.json > tmp.js
▶ echo "console.log(json);" >> tmp.js
▶ nodejs tmp.js
{ contact: { email: 'mail@tomnomnom.com', twitter: '@TomNomNom' },
  github: 'https://github.com/tomnomnom/',
  likes: [ 'code', 'cheese', 'meat' ],
  name: 'Tom' }
```

It's also possible to obtain the `gron` output as JSON stream via the `--json` switch:

```
▶ curl -s http://headers.jsontest.com/ | gron --json
[[],{}]
[["Accept"],"*/*"]
[["Host"],"headers.jsontest.com"]
[["User-Agent"],"curl/7.43.0"]
[["X-Cloud-Trace-Context"],"c70f7bf26661c67d0b9f2cde6f295319/13941186890243645147"]
```

## ungronning

gron can also turn its output back into JSON:

```
▶ gron testdata/two.json | gron -u
{
  "contact": {
    "email": "mail@tomnomnom.com",
    "twitter": "@TomNomNom"
  },
  "github": "https://github.com/tomnomnom/",
  "likes": [
    "code",
    "cheese",
    "meat"
  ],
  "name": "Tom"
}
```

This means you can use gron with `grep` and other tools to modify JSON:

```
▶ gron testdata/two.json | grep likes | gron --ungron
{
  "likes": [
    "code",
    "cheese",
    "meat"
  ]
}
```

Or with JSON stream mode:

```
▶ gron --json testdata/two.json | grep likes | gron --json --ungron
{
  "likes": [
    "code",
    "cheese",
    "meat"
  ]
}
```

To preserve array keys, arrays are padded with `null` when values are missing:

```
▶ gron testdata/two.json | grep likes | grep -v cheese
json.likes = [];
json.likes[0] = "code";
json.likes[2] = "meat";

▶ gron testdata/two.json | grep likes | grep -v cheese | gron --ungron
{
  "likes": [
    "code",
    null,
    "meat"
  ]
}
```

## Command-line Options

```
Transform JSON (from a file, URL, or stdin) into discrete assignments to make it greppable

Usage:
  gron [OPTIONS] [FILE|URL|-]

Options:
  -u, --ungron     Reverse the operation (turn assignments back into JSON)
  -v, --values     Print just the values of provided assignments
  -c, --colorize   Colorize output (default on tty)
  -m, --monochrome Monochrome (don't colorize output)
  -s, --stream     Treat each line of input as a separate JSON object
  -k, --insecure   Disable certificate validation
  -j, --json       Represent gron data as JSON stream
      --no-sort    Don't sort output (faster)
      --version    Print version information

Exit Codes:
  0	OK
  1	Failed to open file
  2	Failed to read input
  3	Failed to form statements
  4	Failed to fetch URL
  5	Failed to parse statements
  6	Failed to encode JSON

Examples:
  gron /tmp/apiresponse.json
  gron http://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users/1 
  curl -s http://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users/1 | gron
  gron http://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users/1 | grep company | gron --ungron
```

## Aliases

It's recommended that you alias `ungron` or `norg` (or both!) to `gron --ungron`:

```bash
alias norg="gron --ungron"
alias ungron="gron --ungron"
```

# Advanced Usage Examples

Although gron's primary purpose is API discovery, when combined with other tools like `grep` it can do some interesting things.

## Examples from the GitHub API

Get the last 5 commits from a repository:

```
▶ gron "https://api.github.com/repos/tomnomnom/gron/commits?per_page=5"
json = [];
json[0] = {};
json[0].author = {};
json[0].author.avatar_url = "https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/58276?v=3";
...
```

Extract just the first commit using `fgrep "json[0]"`:

```
▶ gron "https://api.github.com/repos/tomnomnom/gron/commits?per_page=5" | fgrep "json[0]"
json[0] = {};
json[0].author = {};
json[0].author.avatar_url = "https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/58276?v=3";
...
```

Get just the committer's name and the commit message:

```
▶ gron "https://api.github.com/repos/tomnomnom/gron/commits?per_page=5" | fgrep "json[0]" | egrep "(committer.name|commit.message)"
json[0].commit.committer.name = "Tom Hudson";
json[0].commit.message = "Adds 0.1.7 to changelog";
```

Turn the result back into JSON using `gron --ungron`:

```
▶ gron "https://api.github.com/repos/tomnomnom/gron/commits?per_page=5" | fgrep "json[0]" | egrep "(committer.name|commit.message)" | gron --ungron
[
  {
    "commit": {
      "committer": {
        "name": "Tom Hudson"
      },
      "message": "Adds 0.1.7 to changelog"
    }
  }
]
```

## Flattening Objects

gron preserves the location of values in the JSON, but you can use `sed` to remove keys from the path to flatten objects:

```
▶ gron "https://api.github.com/repos/tomnomnom/gron/commits?per_page=5" | fgrep "json[0]" | egrep "(committer.name|commit.message)" | sed -r "s/(commit|committer)\.//g"
json[0].name = "Tom Hudson";
json[0].message = "Adds 0.1.7 to changelog"
```

With those keys removed, the result is a 'flattened' object:

```
▶ gron "https://api.github.com/repos/tomnomnom/gron/commits?per_page=5" | fgrep "json[0]" | egrep "(committer.name|commit.message)" | sed -r "s/(commit|committer)\.//g" | gron --ungron
[
  {
    "message": "Adds 0.1.7 to changelog",
    "name": "Tom Hudson"
  }
]
```

Process all commits by removing the filter:

```
▶ gron "https://api.github.com/repos/tomnomnom/gron/commits?per_page=5" | egrep "(committer.name|commit.message)" | sed -r "s/(commit|committer)\.//g" | gron --ungron
[
  {
    "message": "Adds 0.1.7 to changelog",
    "name": "Tom Hudson"
  },
  {
    "message": "Refactors natural sort to actually work + be more readable",
    "name": "Tom Hudson"
  },
  ...
]
```

## Including Nested Data

To include nested data like parent commit URLs:

```
▶ gron "https://api.github.com/repos/tomnomnom/gron/commits?per_page=5" | egrep "(committer.name|commit.message|parents.*html_url)" | sed -r "s/(commit|committer)\.//g"

json[0].message = "Adds 0.1.7 to changelog";
json[0].parents[0].html_url = "https://github.com/tomnomnom/gron/commit/48aba5325ece087ae24ab72684851cbe77ce8311";
...
```

Remove the `.html_url` part of the path to simplify the structure:

```
▶ gron "https://api.github.com/repos/tomnomnom/gron/commits?per_page=5" | egrep "(committer.name|commit.message|parents.*html_url)" | sed -r "s/(commit|committer)\.//g" | sed -r "s/\.html_url//"

json[0].message = "Adds 0.1.7 to changelog";
json[0].parents[0] = "https://github.com/tomnomnom/gron/commit/48aba5325ece087ae24ab72684851cbe77ce8311";
...
```


os.chdir("/tmp")
with open("test.json", "w") as f:
    f.write("{\"hello\": \"world\"}")

handler = http.server.SimpleHTTPRequestHandler
httpd = socketserver.TCPServer(("127.0.0.1", 8889), handler)
thread = threading.Thread(target=httpd.serve_forever)
thread.daemon = True
thread.start()

time.sleep(0.1)

p = subprocess.Popen([exe, "http://127.0.0.1:8889/test.json"], stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
out, err = p.communicate()
print("out:", repr(out))
print("err:", repr(err))

httpd.shutdown()
'

import subprocess

tests = [
    # Primitive values
    "json = 123;\n",
    "json = \"hello\";\n",
    "json = true;\n",
    "json = false;\n",
    "json = null;\n",
    # Object with primitive values
    "json = {};\njson.a = 1;\njson.b = \"hello\";\njson.c = true;\njson.d = null;\n",
    # Array with primitive values
    "json = [];\njson[0] = 1;\njson[1] = \"hello\";\njson[2] = true;\n",
    # Array with holes (padded with null)
    "json = [];\njson[0] = 1;\njson[2] = 3;\n",
    # Nested object and array
    "json = {};\njson.a = {};\njson.a.b = [];\njson.a.b[0] = \"nested\";\n",
    # Bracketed object key
    "json = {};\njson[\"key with space\"] = 123;\njson[\"key.with.dot\"] = 456;\n",
]

for i, t in enumerate(tests):
    p = subprocess.Popen(["./executable", "-u"], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
    out, err = p.communicate(input=t)
    print(f"=== Test {i} ===")
    print("Input:\n" + t)
    print("Output:\n" + out)
'"}

import subprocess, json, sys

orig_exe = "./executable"
my_exe = "./my_executable"

def run(exe, flags=[], input_str=None):
    p = subprocess.Popen([exe] + flags, stdin=subprocess.PIPE if input_str is not None else None,
                         stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
    out, err = p.communicate(input=input_str)
    return p.returncode, out, err

tests = [
    # Help and version
    (["--help"], None),
    (["-h"], None),
    (["--version"], None),
    (["--invalid"], None),

    # Standard JSON inputs
    ([], "{\"a\": 1, \"b\": \"hello\", \"c\": true, \"d\": null}"),
    ([], "[1, 2, 3]"),
    ([], "123"),
    ([], "\"hello\""),
    ([], "true"),
    ([], "null"),
    ([], "{}"),
    ([], "[]"),

    # Flags
    (["--no-sort"], "{\"c\": 3, \"a\": 1, \"b\": 2}"),
    (["-j"], "{\"a\": 1, \"b\": [10, 20]}"),
    (["-s"], "{\"a\": 1}\n{\"b\": 2}\n"),
    (["-s", "-j"], "{\"a\": 1}\n{\"b\": 2}\n"),
    (["-c"], "{\"a\": 1, \"b\": \"hello\", \"c\": true}"),
    (["-m"], "{\"a\": 1}"),

    # Ungron (-u)
    (["-u"], "json = {};\njson.a = 1;\njson.b = \"hello\";\n"),
    (["-u"], "json = [];\njson[0] = 1;\njson[2] = 3;\n"),
    (["-u"], "json = 123;\n"),
    (["-u"], "json.a.b = 1;\n"),
    (["-u", "-c"], "json = {};\njson.a = 1;\n"),
    (["-u", "-j"], "[[\"a\"],1]\n"),

    # Values (-v)
    (["-v"], "json.a = 1;\njson.b = \"hello\";\n"),

    # Error cases
    ([], "{invalid}"),
    (["-u"], "invalid statement\n"),
    (["-u"], "json = [];\njson.a = 1;\n"),
    (["nonexistent_file.json"], None),
    (["http://127.0.0.1:99999/invalid"], None),
]

failed = 0
for i, (flags, inp) in enumerate(tests):
    code1, out1, err1 = run(orig_exe, flags, inp)
    code2, out2, err2 = run(my_exe, flags, inp)

    match_code = code1 == code2
    match_out = out1 == out2
    match_err = err1 == err2

    if not (match_code and match_out and match_err):
        failed += 1
        print(f"FAILED Test {i} ({flags}):")
        if not match_code:
            print(f"  Code: orig={code1}, my={code2}")
        if not match_out:
            print(f"  Out orig:\n{repr(out1)}\n  Out my:\n{repr(out2)}")
        if not match_err:
            print(f"  Err orig:\n{repr(err1)}\n  Err my:\n{repr(err2)}")

print(f"\nTotal tests: {len(tests)}, Failed: {failed}")
'"}

                         stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
    out, err = p.communicate(input=input_str)
    return p.returncode, out, err

tests = []

# Complex nested json
complex_json = {
    "string": "Hello, World! \"quotes\" \n \t \\ \u0000",
    "unicode": "åéîøü 🌍 Русский 中文",
    "numbers": [0, -1, 100, 12.34, 1e10, 1.23e-4, -0.0001],
    "booleans": [True, False, None],
    "nested_obj": {
        "empty_obj": {},
        "empty_arr": [],
        "deep": {
            "key.with.dot": "val1",
            "key-with-dash": "val2",
            "key with space": "val3",
            "123numeric": "val4",
            "_valid_id": "val5",
            "$valid_id": "val6",
            "class": "keyword",
            "true": "keyword",
        }
    },
    "array_of_objs": [
        {"id": 1, "name": "Alice"},
        {"id": 2, "name": "Bob", "tags": ["a", "b", "c"]}
    ]
}

tests.append(([], json.dumps(complex_json)))
tests.append((["--no-sort"], json.dumps(complex_json)))
tests.append((["-j"], json.dumps(complex_json)))
tests.append((["-c"], json.dumps(complex_json)))

# Stream mode
stream_input = "\n".join([
    json.dumps({"line": 1, "data": "first"}),
    json.dumps({"line": 2, "data": "second"}),
    json.dumps({"line": 3, "data": "third"})
])
tests.append((["-s"], stream_input))
tests.append((["-s", "-j"], stream_input))
tests.append((["-s", "-c"], stream_input))

# Gron then Ungron roundtrip test
p = subprocess.Popen([orig_exe], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
gron_out, _ = p.communicate(input=json.dumps(complex_json))

tests.append((["-u"], gron_out))
tests.append((["-u", "-c"], gron_out))
tests.append((["-v"], gron_out))

tests.append((["-j", "-u"], json_gron_out))
tests.append((["-j", "-u", "-c"], json_gron_out))

# File input test
tmp_file = "/tmp/test_gron_file.json"
with open(tmp_file, "w") as f:
    f.write(json.dumps(complex_json))

tests.append(([tmp_file], None))

failed = 0
for i, (flags, inp) in enumerate(tests):
    code1, out1, err1 = run(orig_exe, flags, inp)
    code2, out2, err2 = run(my_exe, flags, inp)

    match_code = code1 == code2
    match_out = out1 == out2
    match_err = err1 == err2

    if not (match_code and match_out and match_err):
        failed += 1
        print(f"FAILED Test {i} ({flags}):")
        if not match_code:
            print(f"  Code: orig={code1}, my={code2}")
        if not match_out:
            print(f"  Out orig:\n{repr(out1)}\n  Out my:\n{repr(out2)}")
        if not match_err:
            print(f"  Err orig:\n{repr(err1)}\n  Err my:\n{repr(err2)}")

print(f"\nTotal rigorous tests: {len(tests)}, Failed: {failed}")
'"}

tests.append((["-j", "-u", "-c"], json_gron_out))

import subprocess, json, sys, os

orig_exe = "./executable"
my_exe = "./my_executable"

def run(exe, flags=[], input_str=None):
    p = subprocess.Popen([exe] + flags, stdin=subprocess.PIPE if input_str is not None else None,
                         stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
    out, err = p.communicate(input=input_str)
    return p.returncode, out, err

tests = []

# Complex nested json
complex_json = {
    "string": "Hello, World! \"quotes\" \n \t \\ \u0000",
    "unicode": "åéîøü 🌍 Русский 中文",
    "numbers": [0, -1, 100, 12.34, 1e10, 1.23e-4, -0.0001],
    "booleans": [True, False, None],
    "nested_obj": {
        "empty_obj": {},
        "empty_arr": [],
        "deep": {
            "key.with.dot": "val1",
            "key-with-dash": "val2",
            "key with space": "val3",
            "123numeric": "val4",
            "_valid_id": "val5",
            "$valid_id": "val6",
            "class": "keyword",
            "true": "keyword",
        }
    },
    "array_of_objs": [
        {"id": 1, "name": "Alice"},
        {"id": 2, "name": "Bob", "tags": ["a", "b", "c"]}
    ]
}

tests.append(([], json.dumps(complex_json)))
tests.append((["--no-sort"], json.dumps(complex_json)))
tests.append((["-j"], json.dumps(complex_json)))
tests.append((["-c"], json.dumps(complex_json)))

# Stream mode
stream_input = "\n".join([
    json.dumps({"line": 1, "data": "first"}),
    json.dumps({"line": 2, "data": "second"}),
    json.dumps({"line": 3, "data": "third"})
])
tests.append((["-s"], stream_input))
tests.append((["-s", "-j"], stream_input))
tests.append((["-s", "-c"], stream_input))

# Gron then Ungron roundtrip test
p = subprocess.Popen([orig_exe], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
gron_out, _ = p.communicate(input=json.dumps(complex_json))

tests.append((["-u"], gron_out))
tests.append((["-u", "-c"], gron_out))
tests.append((["-v"], gron_out))

# Gron -j then Ungron -j -u roundtrip test
p = subprocess.Popen([orig_exe, "-j"], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
json_gron_out, _ = p.communicate(input=json.dumps(complex_json))

tests.append((["-j", "-u"], json_gron_out))
tests.append((["-j", "-u", "-c"], json_gron_out))

# File input test
tmp_file = "/tmp/test_gron_file.json"
with open(tmp_file, "w") as f:
    f.write(json.dumps(complex_json))

tests.append(([tmp_file], None))

failed = 0
for i, (flags, inp) in enumerate(tests):
    code1, out1, err1 = run(orig_exe, flags, inp)
    code2, out2, err2 = run(my_exe, flags, inp)

    match_code = code1 == code2
    match_out = out1 == out2
    match_err = err1 == err2

    if not (match_code and match_out and match_err):
        failed += 1
        print(f"FAILED Test {i} ({flags}):")
        if not match_code:
            print(f"  Code: orig={code1}, my={code2}")
        if not match_out:
            print(f"  Out orig:\n{repr(out1)}\n  Out my:\n{repr(out2)}")
        if not match_err:
            print(f"  Err orig:\n{repr(err1)}\n  Err my:\n{repr(err2)}")

print(f"\nTotal rigorous tests: {len(tests)}, Failed: {failed}")
'"}

import subprocess, json, sys, os

orig_exe = "./executable"
my_exe = "./my_executable"

def run(exe, flags=[], input_str=None):
    p = subprocess.Popen([exe] + flags, stdin=subprocess.PIPE if input_str is not None else None,
                         stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
    out, err = p.communicate(input=input_str)
    return p.returncode, out, err

tests = []

# Complex nested json
complex_json = {
    "string": "Hello, World! \"quotes\" \n \t \\ \u0000",
    "unicode": "åéîøü 🌍 Русский 中文",
    "numbers": [0, -1, 100, 12.34, 1e10, 1.23e-4, -0.0001],
    "booleans": [True, False, None],
    "nested_obj": {
        "empty_obj": {},
        "empty_arr": [],
        "deep": {
            "key.with.dot": "val1",
            "key-with-dash": "val2",
            "key with space": "val3",
            "123numeric": "val4",
            "_valid_id": "val5",
            "$valid_id": "val6",
            "class": "keyword",
            "true": "keyword",
        }
    },
    "array_of_objs": [
        {"id": 1, "name": "Alice"},
        {"id": 2, "name": "Bob", "tags": ["a", "b", "c"]}
    ]
}

tests.append(([], json.dumps(complex_json)))
tests.append((["--no-sort"], json.dumps(complex_json)))
tests.append((["-j"], json.dumps(complex_json)))
tests.append((["-c"], json.dumps(complex_json)))

# Stream mode
stream_input = "\n".join([
    json.dumps({"line": 1, "data": "first"}),
    json.dumps({"line": 2, "data": "second"}),
    json.dumps({"line": 3, "data": "third"})
])
tests.append((["-s"], stream_input))
tests.append((["-s", "-j"], stream_input))
tests.append((["-s", "-c"], stream_input))

# Gron then Ungron roundtrip test
p = subprocess.Popen([orig_exe], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
gron_out, _ = p.communicate(input=json.dumps(complex_json))

tests.append((["-u"], gron_out))
tests.append((["-u", "-c"], gron_out))
tests.append((["-v"], gron_out))

# Gron -j then Ungron -j -u roundtrip test
p = subprocess.Popen([orig_exe, "-j"], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
json_gron_out, _ = p.communicate(input=json.dumps(complex_json))

tests.append((["-j", "-u"], json_gron_out))
tests.append((["-j", "-u", "-c"], json_gron_out))

# File input test
tmp_file = "/tmp/test_gron_file.json"
with open(tmp_file, "w") as f:
    f.write(json.dumps(complex_json))

tests.append(([tmp_file], None))

failed = 0
for i, (flags, inp) in enumerate(tests):
    code1, out1, err1 = run(orig_exe, flags, inp)
    code2, out2, err2 = run(my_exe, flags, inp)

    match_code = code1 == code2
    match_out = out1 == out2
    match_err = err1 == err2

    if not (match_code and match_out and match_err):
        failed += 1
        print(f"FAILED Test {i} ({flags}):")
        if not match_code:
            print(f"  Code: orig={code1}, my={code2}")
        if not match_out:
            print(f"  Out orig:\n{repr(out1)}\n  Out my:\n{repr(out2)}")
        if not match_err:
            print(f"  Err orig:\n{repr(err1)}\n  Err my:\n{repr(err2)}")

print(f"\nTotal rigorous tests: {len(tests)}, Failed: {failed}")
'"}

import subprocess, json, sys, os

orig_exe = "./executable"
my_exe = "./my_executable"

def run(exe, flags=[], input_str=None):
    p = subprocess.Popen([exe] + flags, stdin=subprocess.PIPE if input_str is not None else None,
                         stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
    out, err = p.communicate(input=input_str)
    return p.returncode, out, err

tests = []

# Complex nested json
complex_json = {
    "string": "Hello, World! \"quotes\" \n \t \\ \u0000",
    "unicode": "åéîøü 🌍 Русский 中文",
    "numbers": [0, -1, 100, 12.34, 1e10, 1.23e-4, -0.0001],
    "booleans": [True, False, None],
    "nested_obj": {
        "empty_obj": {},
        "empty_arr": [],
        "deep": {
            "key.with.dot": "val1",
            "key-with-dash": "val2",
            "key with space": "val3",
            "123numeric": "val4",
            "_valid_id": "val5",
            "$valid_id": "val6",
            "class": "keyword",
            "true": "keyword",
        }
    },
    "array_of_objs": [
        {"id": 1, "name": "Alice"},
        {"id": 2, "name": "Bob", "tags": ["a", "b", "c"]}
    ]
}

tests.append(([], json.dumps(complex_json)))
tests.append((["-j"], json.dumps(complex_json)))
tests.append((["-c"], json.dumps(complex_json)))

# Stream mode
stream_input = "\n".join([
    json.dumps({"line": 1, "data": "first"}),
    json.dumps({"line": 2, "data": "second"}),
    json.dumps({"line": 3, "data": "third"})
])
tests.append((["-s"], stream_input))
tests.append((["-s", "-j"], stream_input))
tests.append((["-s", "-c"], stream_input))

# Gron then Ungron roundtrip test
p = subprocess.Popen([orig_exe], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
gron_out, _ = p.communicate(input=json.dumps(complex_json))

tests.append((["-u"], gron_out))
tests.append((["-u", "-c"], gron_out))
tests.append((["-v"], gron_out))

# Gron -j then Ungron -j -u roundtrip test
p = subprocess.Popen([orig_exe, "-j"], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
json_gron_out, _ = p.communicate(input=json.dumps(complex_json))

tests.append((["-j", "-u"], json_gron_out))
tests.append((["-j", "-u", "-c"], json_gron_out))

# File input test
tmp_file = "/tmp/test_gron_file.json"
with open(tmp_file, "w") as f:
    f.write(json.dumps(complex_json))

tests.append(([tmp_file], None))

failed = 0
for i, (flags, inp) in enumerate(tests):
    code1, out1, err1 = run(orig_exe, flags, inp)
    code2, out2, err2 = run(my_exe, flags, inp)

    match_code = code1 == code2
    match_out = out1 == out2
    match_err = err1 == err2

    if not (match_code and match_out and match_err):
        failed += 1
        print(f"FAILED Test {i} ({flags}):")
        if not match_code:
            print(f"  Code: orig={code1}, my={code2}")
        if not match_out:
            print(f"  Out orig:\n{repr(out1)}\n  Out my:\n{repr(out2)}")
        if not match_err:
            print(f"  Err orig:\n{repr(err1)}\n  Err my:\n{repr(err2)}")

print(f"\nTotal rigorous tests: {len(tests)}, Failed: {failed}")
'"}
